title: Rafael and the Cipher
premise: Gideon Villalobos, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory makes him both brilliant and haunted, receives two letters about a drowning ruled accidental five years ago: one confessing to murder, the other promising a second death unless he deciphers the cipher hidden in the first. As Gideon reopens the case, he discovers the letters are written by someone with access to the original case file — someone inside the investigation itself. With help from Nadia Okonkwo, a retired archivist who becomes the found family he never had, and Theo, a teenage letter-carrier who saw too much, Gideon races to decode the killer's pattern before the spring tide exposes the body the sea kept. In the end, Gideon traps the killer — his own former mentor, Inspector Reyes — by feeding him a falsified file only a true insider would act on, and the tide gives up what it took: proof that clears an innocent man's name and frees Gideon to claim a family of his own.
about_author: Mara Okafor is a former maritime insurance clerk who spent a decade reading claims from coastal towns where the water keeps its secrets. She writes mysteries about memory and belonging from a small house above a tidal estuary.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On an ordinary Monday, twin letters arrive: one confessing to the drowning of Elena Marsh, the other promising more deaths if the cipher within isn't solved. The emotional beat is dread wrapped in curiosity as Gideon's memory locks every detail into place.

chapters.title: The File That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Gideon pulls the closed Marsh case and finds pages subtly altered since he last read them. His POV; the beat is vertigo — his perfect memory versus a record that lies.

chapters.title: Cipher of Tides
chapters.summary: Gideon studies the confession's embedded cipher, recognizing tidal tables as its key. He visits the coastal archive and meets Nadia Okonkwo, who corrects his chart-reading without being asked. Beat: reluctant connection.

chapters.title: What the Sea Kept
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. She remembers Elena Marsh, a lighthouse keeper's daughter who drowned five years ago, and shares what official files omit. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, and the first hint of alliance.

chapters.title: Second Letter
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives naming a date and a victim: harbor pilot Cormac Bell. Gideon realizes the killer is running a countdown. His POV; beat: urgency sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: The Insider Problem
chapters.summary: Gideon lists everyone with access to the original file and finds the list uncomfortably short — including his old mentor, Inspector Reyes. Beat: betrayal foreshadowed, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Cormac Bell's Last Shift
chapters.summary: Theo, a sharp-eyed teen mail carrier, mentions delivering a strange parcel to Bell. Gideon interviews Bell, who is evasive and terrified. Beat: a clock starting to tick audibly.

chapters.title: Decoding the First Death
chapters.summary: Nadia and Gideon crack the cipher's outer layer: it encodes not a confession but coordinates. They visit the cove at low tide and find nothing — yet. Beat: frustration edged with wonder at their growing partnership.

chapters.title: Reyes Warns Him Off
chapters.summary: Inspector Reyes appears, urging Gideon to drop it, citing his own breakdown after the Marsh case. Gideon reads the warning as either protection or threat. Beat: unease.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Saw Too Much
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He admits he saw someone burning papers near the archive dumpster — someone wearing an inspector's coat. Beat: fear and the weight of being believed.

chapters.title: Cormac Bell, Missing
chapters.summary: Bell vanishes on the date named in the second letter. Gideon finds Bell's boat adrift, engine warm. Beat: failure and guilt — he was hours late.

chapters.title: Photographic Ghosts
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: young Gideon's memory made him a prodigy and an outcast; Reyes took him under his wing. Beat: tenderness toward the man he may now have to destroy.

chapters.title: The Altered Page
chapters.summary: Gideon reconstructs the original file from memory and identifies exactly which page was swapped — a tide log placing a witness at the cove. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Nadia's Archive War
chapters.summary: Nadia fights bureaucratic stonewalling to access sealed records, revealing she was pushed out of the archive years ago for asking similar questions. Beat: righteous anger, shared exile.

chapters.title: Third Letter
chapters.summary: The killer writes directly to Gideon, praising his memory and taunting: 'You remember everything except what matters.' Beat: psychological violation — the killer knows him intimately.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
chapters.summary: Gideon tracks down Elena's father, now dying, who whispers that Elena was afraid of a policeman. Beat: heartbreak and confirmation.

chapters.title: Suspect Web
chapters.summary: Gideon maps the case: three insiders had file access, but alibis for the night of the third letter eliminate two. Beat: the net tightening around one name he refuses to speak.

chapters.title: Tide Tables and Lies
chapters.summary: Nadia spots that the cipher's tidal data comes from next year's tables — meaning the killer plans a final act at the spring tide, three weeks out. Beat: deadline crystallized.

chapters.title: Theo Follows the Coat
chapters.summary: Theo tails the figure in the inspector's coat and photographs him — the image is blurred, inconclusive, but the gait matches Reyes. Beat: dread made visual.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Pier
chapters.summary: Gideon confronts Reyes, who denies everything and produces an alibi — then quietly warns, 'Whoever wrote those letters wants you to think it's me.' Beat: doubt reinstalled.

chapters.title: The Fourth Letter Is Blank
chapters.summary: An envelope arrives containing only a pressed sprig of sea lavender — Elena's favorite flower. Gideon realizes the killer is performing grief, or mocking his. Beat: quiet horror.

chapters.title: Breaking Point
chapters.summary: Sleepless, Gideon's memory turns traitor, replaying Bell's boat and Elena's file on loop. Nadia finds him at dawn and forces him to eat, rest, talk. Beat: vulnerability; found family solidifying.

chapters.title: What Theo Knew All Along
chapters.summary: Theo confesses he held back a detail: the burner-paper figure dropped a key fob stamped with the marine unit's insignia. Beat: trust repaired through honesty.

chapters.title: The Marine Unit Locker
chapters.summary: Gideon and Nadia trace the fob to a decommissioned locker rented under a dead man's name — the same alias used on the Marsh file's missing page. Beat: the puzzle clicking.

chapters.title: Inside the Locker
chapters.summary: They open the locker: Elena's journal, a duplicate cipher key, and photographs of Gideon himself taken over months. Beat: violation deepening into resolve.

chapters.title: Elena's Journal
chapters.summary: Elena's own words reveal she witnessed a smuggling operation run through the harbor and reported it to a trusted inspector. Beat: the motive surfacing — silencing, not madness.

chapters.title: The Trusted Inspector
chapters.summary: The journal names no one, but Gideon's memory supplies the detail: only one inspector had access to her report. Reyes again — or someone wearing his authority. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Frame Job
chapters.summary: Anonymous tips land Reyes's home address with police; someone is accelerating the endgame by burning the mentor. Gideon suspects misdirection. Beat: race against a rigged game.

chapters.title: Reyes on the Run
chapters.summary: Reyes flees, calling Gideon at midnight: 'I taught you to read files. Read mine.' He leaves a key to his personal case notes. Beat: tragic inversion — hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Mentor's Notes
chapters.summary: Reyes's private notes reveal he suspected the smuggling ring for years and altered the file himself — to protect a witness, not to bury evidence. Beat: relief and new confusion.

chapters.title: The Real Insider
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing Reyes's notes with the cipher, Gideon identifies the true author: Deputy Coroner Silas Vane, who certified Elena's drowning and controlled the file's chain of custody. Beat: revelation with icy calm.

chapters.title: Vane's Perfect Record
chapters.summary: Vane has certified eleven coastal drownings in nine years, each backed by flawless paperwork. Gideon realizes the cipher letters were bait to draw out anyone still investigating. Beat: horror at elegant evil.

chapters.title: Trap Design
chapters.summary: Gideon drafts a falsified file — a fabricated witness placed at the spring-tide cove — and lets it leak through channels only Vane monitors. Beat: the hunter setting his hook.

chapters.title: Bait Taken
chapters.summary: The false page vanishes from the system within hours; Vane requests the tide charts for the cove. Gideon watches the trap close via Nadia's archive logs. Beat: grim satisfaction.

chapters.title: Spring Tide Eve
chapters.summary: Storm warnings rise with the tide. Gideon stations Theo safely away, arms himself with recordings, and waits at the cove with Nadia watching the road. Beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: The Cove at High Water
chapters.summary: Vane arrives to move the final evidence before the tide exposes it. Gideon confronts him; Vane, unmasked, speaks with chilling pride about order, paperwork, and the sea as the perfect filing cabinet. Beat: climax of wills.

chapters.title: What the Water Gives Back
chapters.summary: As Vane moves to silence Gideon, the storm surge uncovers a weighted crate — Bell, alive, half-drowned, having escaped his bonds. Vane hesitates; police lights crest the dune. Beat: salvation from the very sea.

chapters.title: Confession, Third Draft
chapters.summary: Confronted with the recovered crate, Bell's testimony, and the forged-file sting, Vane unravels with bureaucratic precision, dictating his own confession like a form. Beat: catharsis without triumph.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Reyes returns to face inquiry; Elena's name is cleared; Theo is formally thanked and unofficially adopted into Sunday dinners at Nadia's table. Beat: grief settling into gratitude.

chapters.title: The Memory He Chooses
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, epilogue. Standing at the cove at low tide, he realizes memory is not a cage but a keepsake box. He keeps the blank fourth letter, presses sea lavender inside, and goes home to his family. Beat: peace earned.
